answer: AI agents resist Sybil attacks through verifiable identity staking and secure enclave attestation. Each agent must stake scarce capital, acting as a crystal of value, while its operating environment's cryptographic kernel provides identity integrity via TEE attestation. This makes forging multiple identities prohibitively expensive; an attacker must acquire significant capital and unique hardware for each. Each verified agent effectively occupies a distinct computational knoll, making Sybil generation economically infeasible and resource-constrained.
